title: Baby Dodds in his later years
summary: He last saw Dodds at the Hunt Club in Chicago, weakened by illness but still fast on quick tunes.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Because when Baby was... Mm-hmm. Uh, did you ever see Baby playing in later years?
The only time I, last time I saw Baby play was when he rushed me up at, uh, at this nightclub in Chicago.

Because you see, he was well known around there, you know, because he used to play in different places. Yeah. Well, that was when he was sick. He was kind of sick then. Oh, yeah. But every time we went out to Chicago before he died, he always came by and I let him set in. Yeah. And then, at that time his wrist was going bad then. Yeah. And I would let him try to work his wrist some, you know, but... Yeah. But it didn't, it didn't have to do any good to him. No. Until he'd taken that stroke and he had to go to the hospital and that was it.
But he could still play, I guess, pretty well. Yeah, he was playing pretty good, fast numbers, but he couldn't do nothing with slow numbers. No.
No. He did pretty good with fast numbers, but slow numbers he was handicapped. Yeah, I see. Because he couldn't make the press rolls like this. No, he couldn't make the rolls like he wanted to.
And the baby never changed, say, right from the time you first knew him, you know, he still playing more or less the same drum.
No, he still was the same identical thing.
